name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,266

clue.text: Daughter is last to finish food

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, so only the closing letter of the next word is kept

blocks.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
taken as written
the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: A daughter dawdles over dinner and is the last one still eating.
explanation.walkthrough: D is the usual abbreviation for daughter, as in family trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish is a prepared item of cooking served at a meal, so the word stands for something eaten.

clue.text: US soldier set up facilities in simple dwelling

indicators.note: in a down clue, setting something up raises it so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: GI is the familiar name for an American soldier
loo is British slang for a toilet, the 'facilities'

explanation.surface: An American soldier builds a latrine at a basic shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Facilities' is a polite word for toilets, and loo is the everyday British word for one; in a down entry 'set up' turns a word to read upward.
explanation.definitionFit: An Inuit snow house is a basic shelter built from blocks of packed snow, a plain home.

clue.text: Dropping litter and becoming anxious

blocks.note: first meaning: a cat giving birth to a brood of young
second meaning: a British idiom for getting into a nervous state

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping litter' reads like tossing rubbish, but to drop a litter is for an animal to give birth. The second sense is a British idiom for being very nervous or agitated.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat delivering young is literally doing this, and the same phrase is British slang for working oneself into a state of panic.

clue.text: Extremely demure uniform characteristic of speaker

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only the outermost letters are kept

blocks.note: the first and last letters of this word
livery is the distinctive uniform worn by servants or staff

explanation.surface: A very modest outfit becomes the trademark of a public speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uniform' is not the NATO letter U here; it is a noun meaning official dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A speaker's manner of voicing words, the pace, tone and style of oratory, is called their delivery.

clue.text: Foppish fellow departs with Yankee

blocks.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs
'and' means along with
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A vain, fashionable man leaves accompanied by an American.
explanation.walkthrough: D for departs comes from railway timetables, and Yankee is the radio code word for Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A dandy is a man excessively devoted to his clothes and appearance, which is exactly what foppish describes.

clue.text: Earl abroad covers the skin

indicators.note: something abroad is out of its usual place, so the letters wander into a new order
to cover something is to wrap around it, so one group surrounds another

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nobleman travelling overseas wraps up his hide against the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earl' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it is only letters to be jumbled; the jumbled result is then split to hold the article.
explanation.definitionFit: Leather is tanned animal hide, and 'skin' can mean the processed hide of an animal as well as living skin.

clue.text: State service provider missing one location in Surrey

indicators.note: something missing is absent, so a letter is dropped from the word before it

blocks.note: Virginia is a US state
a waiter provides service at table
I is the Roman numeral one, and it is removed

explanation.surface: A government-run utility company loses a site somewhere in Surrey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State service provider' looks like one public body, but it splits into a US state and a waiter. Surrey is an English county south-west of London; Virginia Water is a village there.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginia Water is a real village and lake in the English county of Surrey, near Windsor Great Park.

clue.text: Enlisted chief journalist to probe Ripon criminal

indicators.note: a criminal is crooked, so these letters are bent out of their order
a probe pushes inside something, so one piece goes into the middle of another

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
ED is short for editor, the chief journalist on a paper

explanation.surface: A newly recruited senior reporter is sent to investigate a crook from Ripon.
explanation.walkthrough: Ripon is a small cathedral city in North Yorkshire; its letters become ROPIN and ED goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To be roped in is to be persuaded or recruited to take part, so it matches enlisted as a past participle.

clue.text: Alison failed to secure EV around European country

indicators.note: something that has failed has broken down, so the letters fall apart and reassemble
turned around means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards
to secure is to hold fast, so one group grips another inside it

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written, an electric vehicle

explanation.surface: Alison couldn't get hold of an electric vehicle anywhere on the continent.
explanation.walkthrough: EV is the common abbreviation for an electric vehicle, but here it is just two letters to be flipped; three separate signals act on one short clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Slovenia is a nation in central Europe bordering Italy, Austria, Hungary and Croatia.

clue.text: Periodically, fruit pie’s ready to eat

indicators.note: something done periodically happens at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: Every so often a fruit pie comes out of the oven ready to serve.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s is read as 'is', linking wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit that is fully matured and fit for eating is described as ripe.

clue.text: Foreign nobleman encounters unknown shire

blocks.note: a count is a continental European noble, the equivalent of an earl
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A visiting aristocrat comes across an unfamiliar rural district.
explanation.walkthrough: Britain has earls rather than counts, which is why the count is 'foreign'. X, Y and Z are the usual unknowns from algebra.
explanation.definitionFit: Shire is the old English word for an administrative region, now generally called a county.

clue.text: Aggressive dog’s curfew half ignored

indicators.note: ignoring half of something leaves only the other half, so part of the word is dropped

blocks.note: the first half of this word, the second half being dropped

explanation.surface: A snarling dog pays no attention to the night-time curfew.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A cur is a mongrel, especially a snappish or vicious one, so it suits a hostile hound.

clue.text: Maybe Bob ate duck around Ireland

indicators.note: to sit around something is to surround it, so one piece goes outside another

blocks.note: to have a meal is to eat it, so 'had' can mean ate
IR is an abbreviation for Ireland
a duck is a zero score in cricket, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A man called Bob perhaps had duck for dinner somewhere in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob looks like a man's name, but it is a short haircut. In cricket a duck is a score of nothing, so it gives O.
explanation.definitionFit: A bob is one example of a hairstyle, a short even cut, hence the 'Maybe' marking an example.

clue.text: Boxer wobbling, hurt, finally beaten amid cheers

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the closing letter of the word is used
amid means in the middle of, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: rocky means unsteady
to mar is to damage or spoil
ciao, like cheers, is a casual goodbye
the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: A battered prizefighter, staggering and in pain, finally goes down while the crowd roars.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheers is a British way of saying goodbye as well as a toast, so it matches the Italian farewell CIAO.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocky Marciano was the American heavyweight champion of the 1950s who retired unbeaten, a famous prizefighter.

clue.text: Greek character’s minor company briefly reorganised

indicators.note: reorganising puts things into a fresh arrangement, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
CO is the short form of company

explanation.surface: A Greek man's small firm has been restructured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' tells you to use the abbreviation CO, which joins the other five letters for the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Omicron is the fifteenth letter of the Greek alphabet, and 'character' here means a written letter.

clue.text: Some athlete ran impulsively up tower

indicators.note: some means a part of what follows, so the letters lie within the given words
in a down clue, going up means reading from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, all of the second, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A sprinter dashes on a whim up a tall building.
explanation.walkthrough: The run TERANIM sits across three words and is read upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A minaret is the slender tower of a mosque from which the call to prayer is made.

clue.text: Duke supporting old English verse

indicators.note: in a down clue, a supporting piece sits beneath another, so it comes after it

blocks.note: O is a common abbreviation for old
D is the abbreviation for duke
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An aristocrat backs traditional English poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: Duke is written first but sits under old in this down entry, then English comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: An ode is a lyric poem, usually addressed to a subject, so it is a piece of poetry.

clue.text: Points affected another part of engine

definitions.note: 'another' nods to the neighbouring engine-themed entries; the answer is simply a part of an engine

indicators.note: something affected has been altered or influenced, so the letters are changed in order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Contact points have had a knock-on effect on a different engine component.
explanation.walkthrough: Points are themselves engine parts (ignition points), which is why the surface hangs together.
explanation.definitionFit: A piston is the sliding cylinder component driven by combustion inside an internal-combustion motor.

clue.text: Formal attire boyfriend, southeast Asian, picked up

indicators.note: to pick up a signal is to hear it, so the words are taken by their sound

blocks.note: a beau is an old-fashioned word for a boyfriend
a Thai is a person from Thailand in southeast Asia

explanation.surface: A woman's boyfriend, from Southeast Asia, is collected wearing evening dress.
explanation.walkthrough: BEAU sounds like BOW and THAI sounds like TIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bow tie is the neckwear worn with a dinner jacket at black-tie events, an item of evening dress.

clue.text: Head bishop formerly

blocks.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
once means at some time in the past

explanation.surface: A man who used to lead the diocese as its senior cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head bishop' reads as a single senior churchman, but the first word is the definition. Bonce is British slang for the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonce is informal British slang for a person's skull or noggin.

clue.text: Pub exactly what’s needed, don’t you think?

blocks.note: an inn is a pub
'it' can mean the very thing, as in 'that's it'

explanation.surface: Someone suggests a pub is just the thing and asks for agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: Innit is British street slang, a contraction of 'isn't it', tagged onto a remark to seek agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang tag is used at the end of a statement to invite agreement, just like asking a listener's opinion.

clue.text: Unrestrained Republican in charge

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for Republican
a fee is a charge for a service

explanation.surface: A wild Republican politician has been put in command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In charge' looks like one phrase meaning responsible; it splits into the container signal and a word for a payment.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unrestrained is not held back or confined, which is to be at liberty.

clue.text: Band start to tout single that’s often played on phones

definitions.note: a descriptive clause standing for the noun

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: a ring is a circular band
the opening letter of this word
one is a single unit

explanation.surface: A group begins promoting its new release, a tune heard on mobiles everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' and 'single' sound like pop music, but they are a ring and the number one.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringtone is the sound or short tune a mobile makes to announce an incoming call.

clue.text: Liqueur developed in estate

indicators.note: something developed has been worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spirit has been produced on a country property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word but its letters are part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Anisette is a sweet aniseed-flavoured spirit, one type of liqueur.

clue.text: Schedule artist retains over time

indicators.note: to retain is to keep hold of, so one piece holds others inside

blocks.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a recognised artist
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A painter keeps his timetable despite running late.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts in London. An over is a set of six balls in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A rota is a British word for a roster listing who does which duty and when.
